what: Trip.com Group is China's largest online travel company. It books hotels, flights and packages for Chinese travellers through Trip.com and Ctrip, and owns Skyscanner, the flight metasearch site used worldwide.
customers: Chinese domestic and outbound travellers, plus international users of Trip.com and Skyscanner.
moat: The dominant booking position in the Chinese travel market, with hotel supply relationships and a customer base that is hard for foreign platforms to reach.
risks: Chinese consumer spending has been uneven
Chinese regulatory and geopolitical risk affects US-listed Chinese shares
Outbound travel recovery depends on flight capacity and visa policy
Meituan competes aggressively in domestic hotel booking
opportunities: Revenue grew about 22% last year and about 45% a year over three years
Operating margin of 25% with cash of $12 billion against $4 billion of debt
Chinese outbound travel is still below pre-2020 levels, leaving room to recover
watch: Outbound travel bookings and international platform growth.
